clue.text: Fancy being awake!

parts.note: a fantasy you have while you are not asleep: dreaming in the daytime, eyes open

explanation.definitionFit: A reverie or fantasy indulged while conscious is the waking counterpart of a night-time dream.

clue.text: Eggs being up, about to serve fruit

indicators.note: in a down clue, a word that is up reads from the bottom, so it is turned backwards

parts.note: OVA is the Latin plural for eggs
CA, short for circa, means about
DO means serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'

explanation.surface: Breakfast eggs are on, and a fruit is about to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'being up' reads the eggs upwards; 'to' is only a link, and 'serve' is the sense of 'that will do'.
explanation.definitionFit: The avocado is the pear-shaped fruit of a tropical tree, eaten as a savoury.

clue.text: Application from former coach

definitions.meaning: steady, careful hard work or effort
a public stagecoach of old, especially in France

explanation.definitionFit: The word means persistent effort, and was also the name of the old horse-drawn public coach, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Players leave being out of tune badly

parts.note: EX means out of or former, as in an ex-partner who is out of the picture

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of tune are played wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Musicians walk off the stage because their playing has gone out of tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Players' are actors, not musicians; 'badly' scrambles the tune, and 'being' and 'of' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin stage direction tells actors that they all go off the stage.

clue.text: Where the ayes, say, may be seen dividing left from right

definitions.text: Where the ayes, say, may be seen dividing left from right

parts.words: Where the ayes, say, may be seen dividing left from right
parts.note: ayes stands for eyes, the reflective cat's eyes set along the centre line of a road; politically it also suggests a moderate position between left and right

explanation.walkthrough: Cat's eyes are reflective studs set in a road's centre line; 'ayes' pretends to be about parliamentary votes.
explanation.definitionFit: The centre of a highway separates the lanes, just as moderate politics sits between the two wings.

clue.text: Field made smaller

definitions.meaning: a pitch or stadium area for sport
reduced to small pieces, as coffee beans are milled

explanation.definitionFit: A sports pitch is a playing area, and milled coffee has been crushed fine, so both senses fit.

clue.text: Was it swept under King of Phrygia's carpet?

definitions.text: Was it swept under King of Phrygia's carpet?

parts.words: Was it swept under King of Phrygia's carpet?
parts.note: the King of Phrygia is Midas, whose touch turned everything to precious metal, so even his household dirt would be precious

explanation.walkthrough: Midas, king of Phrygia, turned all he touched to gold, so the dirt in his house would be gold too.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine particles of the precious metal, also a phrase for anything rare and valuable.

clue.text: Pursuer involved in take-over bid

definitions.note: describes a person, one engaged in grabbing power

indicators.note: involved means twisted or tangled, so the letters of Pursuer are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a company is part of a takeover attempt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges PURSUER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who seizes a throne or position without right is caught up in an illegitimate attempt at control.

clue.text: Met spider in mess, made complaint

indicators.note: in a mess means jumbled, so the letters of Met spider are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone meets a spider in an untidy room and grumbles about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in mess' rearranges the nine letters of MET SPIDER; 'made' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint is an illness, and this is a viral disease of dogs.

clue.text: Dog taking bite out of miner's backside

indicators.note: taking a bite out of a word removes a little of it
the backside of the word is its last letter, which is the part bitten off

parts.note: a COLLIER is a coal miner

explanation.surface: A dog bites a coal miner on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking bite out of' and 'backside' remove the final R of COLLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheepdog breed of Scottish origin.

clue.text: No go area for early seamen

definitions.text: No go area for early seamen

parts.words: No go area for early seamen
parts.note: a stretch of ocean near the equator where sailing ships of old were becalmed and could not move

explanation.definitionFit: The equatorial belt of calm winds where sailing ships were stuck for weeks.

clue.text: Sort of seat that is wobbly?

definitions.text: Sort of seat that is wobbly?

parts.words: Sort of seat that is wobbly?
parts.note: a parliamentary constituency held by a small majority, so it might fall, rather than a rickety chair

explanation.walkthrough: A seat is a parliamentary constituency here, not furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A constituency won by a narrow majority is at risk of changing hands at the next election.

clue.text: Becoming hollow

parts.note: becoming means attractive, so a fetching little hollow, as in the cheek or chin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' looks like 'turning into' but means attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: A small attractive indentation in the cheek or chin, especially when smiling.

clue.text: Tell of Monte Christo

definitions.meaning: to number things, as a bank teller does
the title of Dumas's hero, Edmond Dantes, a nobleman's rank

explanation.definitionFit: To tell money is to number it, and Dumas's novel names its hero as a nobleman of that rank.

clue.text: Horner later in life as last of the nigger minstrels?

definitions.text: Horner later in life as last of the nigger minstrels?

parts.words: Horner later in life as last of the nigger minstrels?
parts.note: Little Jack Horner of the nursery rhyme sat in a corner; in old blackface minstrel shows the performer at each end of the line had this title

explanation.walkthrough: The clue uses a racist term from its era for the old blackface minstrel shows; the end performers in the line had this name.
explanation.definitionFit: In a minstrel show the comic at either end of the semicircle of performers bore this title.

clue.text: Hazardous spot for Cheddar gorge

parts.note: gorge is a verb, to eat greedily on cheese, not the famous Somerset ravine, Cheddar Gorge

explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a famous limestone ravine in Somerset, England; here 'gorge' means to stuff oneself with the cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: A baited trap that snaps on a rodent nibbling cheese.

clue.text: Strike perhaps at the Oval

parts.note: a trial of a match, as in striking one, read as the international cricket fixture played at the London ground

explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground that hosts international five-day games; striking a match might be a test of it.
explanation.definitionFit: An international cricket fixture, often played at the Oval.

clue.text: American flier has to waste time

parts.note: to blue money is British slang for squandering it
BIRD is slang for time spent in prison

explanation.surface: An American pilot has time to kill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has to' is a link; to blue money is British slang for wasting it, and doing bird is serving a prison sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: A small North American thrush with bright plumage.

clue.text: Sort of true Liberal spurning academic status — a real gem

indicators.note: sort of signals that the letters of true Liberal are sorted into a new order
spurning means rejecting, so those letters are left out of the pool

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A genuine Liberal who turns down an academic honour is a real treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove R and A from TRUE LIBERAL and rearrange the remaining nine letters; 'a real' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pink or red variety of tourmaline, prized as a precious stone.

clue.text: Colourful show opening in the Spring

definitions.text: Colourful show opening in the Spring

parts.words: Colourful show opening in the Spring
parts.note: not a theatre production but flowers unfolding on trees in springtime

explanation.definitionFit: The mass of flowers on fruit trees in spring is a bright display that unfolds.

clue.text: Shoot out of bed in basket

definitions.text: Shoot out of bed in basket

parts.words: Shoot out of bed in basket
parts.note: a willow twig cut from a bed of such willows, woven into baskets

explanation.walkthrough: 'Shoot out of bed' suggests leaping up in the morning; the bed is a plantation of willows.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliable willow twig used for wickerwork, grown in beds.

clue.text: Get ready to travel with enthusiasm

definitions.meaning: to board a railway carriage before a journey
French '...', in full swing or in high spirits

explanation.definitionFit: To get aboard a rail carriage is preparing to set off, and the French phrase means under way with spirit.

clue.text: Found around upper-class house?

indicators.note: around means the word for Found goes around the letter for upper-class

parts.note: to found a firm is to START it
U is the abbreviation for upper-class, as opposed to non-U

explanation.surface: Someone sets up a grand house for the upper classes.
explanation.walkthrough: A royal house is a dynasty; the Stuarts ruled Scotland and later England.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal dynasty that ruled Scotland and then England.

clue.text: Turn off right to make progress?

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the letter for right is dropped

parts.note: to REVOLVE is to turn round

explanation.surface: A driver turns off to the right to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' drops the R from REVOLVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To develop gradually is to advance step by step.

clue.text: Reckon one set perhaps to finish game

indicators.note: perhaps suggests one possible arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
MATE, checkmate, finishes a game of chess

explanation.surface: Someone works out the score of a tennis set before the match ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I and SET as ESTI; 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reckon is to judge or calculate roughly.

clue.text: Doctor's capital means of bloodletting

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, a doctor, plus the possessive S
QUITO is the capital city of Ecuador

explanation.surface: A doctor in a capital city practises bloodletting.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: A biting insect that draws blood from its victims.

clue.text: Another body of stars?

definitions.meaning: a spirit double said in occultism to exist alongside the physical self
relating to the heavens and the celestial lights

explanation.definitionFit: In occult belief one has a second, spirit self beyond the physical, and the adjective also means relating to the heavens.

clue.text: Arkwright's descendant a skilled hunter

definitions.meaning: the builder of the Ark was Noah, and this figure was his great-grandson in Genesis
Genesis calls him a mighty hunter, so his name means any expert huntsman

explanation.walkthrough: 'Arkwright' looks like the inventor Richard Arkwright, but means Noah, the builder of the Ark.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical great-grandson of Noah, called a mighty hunter, gave his name to any keen huntsman.

clue.text: Leaving a rural occupation

definitions.meaning: the farm work of digging and clearing drainage channels

explanation.definitionFit: To abandon something is slang for dumping it, and digging drainage channels is farm labour.
